translations.idiomatic: At first officials still submitted congratulatory memorials; later the reports became routine, and not every case received congratulations.

sentences.zh: 時朱勝非爲京東提舉學事，行部至密州界，見縣令部數百夫入山采芝。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Shengfei was commissioner for educational affairs in the Jingdong circuit; on an inspection tour reaching the border of Mizhou, he saw the county magistrate marshaling several hundred laborers to enter the mountains and gather lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Shengfei, commissioner for educational affairs in the Jingdong circuit, was on an inspection tour when he reached the border of Mizhou and saw the county magistrate mustering several hundred laborers to enter the mountains and gather lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 彌漫山谷，皆芝菌也。

translations.literal: They filled the valleys and hills—all were lingzhi fungi.
translations.idiomatic: They filled the valleys and hills—nothing but lingzhi fungi.

sentences.zh: 或附木石，或出平地，有一本數十葉，層疊高大，衆色鹹備。

translations.literal: Some clung to trees and stones, some sprang from level ground; single plants bore dozens of leaves, layered and towering, every color represented.
translations.idiomatic: Some clung to trees and stones, others sprang from level ground; single plants bore dozens of leaves, layered and towering, every color represented.

sentences.zh: 郡守李文仲采及三十萬本，每萬本作一綱入貢。

translations.literal: The prefect Li Wenzhong collected as many as three hundred thousand plants, sending tribute in batches of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Li Wenzhong collected as many as three hundred thousand plants and sent tribute in batches of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 文仲尋進職，授本道轉運使。

translations.literal: Wenzhong was soon promoted and appointed transport commissioner for the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong was soon promoted and appointed transport commissioner for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年九月癸卯，權知密州杜彥獻芝草，五葉，如人指掌，色赤而澤。

translations.literal: On guimao in the ninth month of the second year of Jianyan, Du Yan, acting prefect of Mizhou, presented lingzhi grass of five leaves shaped like a human palm, crimson and lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the ninth month of the second year of Jianyan, Du Yan, acting prefect of Mizhou, presented lingzhi grass of five leaves shaped like a human palm, crimson and lustrous.

sentences.zh: 宰臣黃潛善奏：「色符火德，形像股肱之瑞。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Huang Qianshan memorialized: "The color matches the virtue of Fire; the form resembles an omen of the emperor's supporting arms."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Huang Qianshan memorialized: "The color matches the virtue of Fire, and the form resembles an omen of the emperor's supporting arms."

sentences.zh: 高宗不啟視，卻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong did not open it to look and refused it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong would not even open it to look and refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年七月乙未，浙西安撫大使劉光世以枯秸生穗奏瑞。

translations.literal: On yiwei in the seventh month of the first year of Shaoxing, Liu Guangshi, grand coordinator of Zhexi, memorialized an auspicious sign: dry stalks bearing grain heads.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the seventh month of the first year of Shaoxing, Liu Guangshi, grand coordinator of Zhexi, memorialized as an auspicious sign dry stalks that had sprouted grain heads.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「朕在潛邸，梁間生芝草，官僚皆欲上聞，朕手碎之，不欲寶此奇怪。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "When I was in my princely residence, lingzhi grew between the rafters. The officials all wished to report it, but I crushed it with my own hand—I did not wish to treasure such strangeness."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said: "When I was in my princely residence, lingzhi grew between the rafters. The officials all wished to report it, but I crushed it with my own hand—I did not wish to treasure such strangeness."

sentences.zh: 乃卻之。

translations.literal: And he refused the offering.
translations.idiomatic: And he refused the offering.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月辛未，瀘州天雨豆，近草妖也。

translations.literal: On xinwei in the first month of the sixteenth year, beans rained from the sky in Luzhou—nearly a grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the first month of the sixteenth year, beans rained from the sky in Luzhou—a grass prodigy portent.

sentences.zh: 十六年，梅州孔子廟生芝。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, lingzhi grew at the Temple of Confucius in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, lingzhi appeared at the Temple of Confucius in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，紹興府學御書下生芝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, lingzhi grew beneath the imperial calligraphy at the Shaoxing prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, lingzhi grew beneath the imperial calligraphy at the Shaoxing prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 番陽縣石門民家籬竹生重萼牡丹，又民家灶鼎生金色蓮華。

translations.literal: At a commoner's home in Shimen, Poyang county, hedge bamboo produced a double-petaled peony; at another home a golden lotus grew from a cooking hearth.
translations.idiomatic: At a commoner's home in Shimen, Poyang county, hedge bamboo bore a double-petaled peony; at another home a golden lotus sprang from a cooking hearth.

sentences.zh: 房州治所彩山下生萱。

translations.literal: At the foot of Cai Mountain below the seat of government in Fangzhou, daylilies grew.
translations.idiomatic: Daylilies appeared at the foot of Cai Mountain below the seat of government in Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬州、虔州放生池生蓮，皆同蒂異萼。

translations.literal: Lotuses grew in the life-release ponds of Wanzhou and Qianzhou, all sharing one stem but with separate calyxes.
translations.idiomatic: Lotuses grew in the life-release ponds of Wanzhou and Qianzhou, all sharing one stem with separate calyxes.

sentences.zh: 二十三年六月，汀州生蓮，同蒂異萼者十有二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year, lotuses grew in Tingzhou; twelve shared one stem with separate calyxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year, lotuses appeared in Tingzhou; twelve bore a shared stem with separate calyxes.

sentences.zh: 二十五年五月，太室楹生芝九莖，秦檜帥百官觀之，稱賀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year, nine stalks of lingzhi grew on a pillar of the Grand Chamber. Qin Hui led the officials to view them and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year, nine stalks of lingzhi grew on a pillar of the Grand Chamber. Qin Hui led the officials to view them and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 勾龍廉、沈中立以獻頌遷擢，周麟之請繪之鹵簿行旗。

translations.literal: Gou Longlian and Shen Zhongli were promoted for presenting eulogies; Zhou Linzhi requested that it be painted on the imperial procession banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Longlian and Shen Zhongli were promoted for presenting eulogies, and Zhou Linzhi requested that it be painted on the imperial procession banners.

sentences.zh: 檜孫禮部侍郎塤請以黎州甘露降草木、道州連理木、鎮江府瑞瓜、南安軍瑞蓮、嚴、信州瑞芝悉圖之旗。

translations.literal: Qin's grandson, Vice Minister of Rites Sun, requested that the banners also depict sweet dew descending on plants in Lizhou, joined-trunk trees in Daozhou, the auspicious melon of Zhenjiang prefecture, the auspicious lotus of Nan'an army, and auspicious lingzhi from Yan and Xin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's grandson Sun, vice minister of rites, asked that the banners also depict sweet dew descending on plants in Lizhou, joined-trunk trees in Daozhou, the auspicious melon of Zhenjiang prefecture, the auspicious lotus of Nan'an army, and auspicious lingzhi from Yan and Xin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是冬，檜薨，高宗曰：「比年四方奏瑞，文飾取悅，若信州林機奏秦檜父祠堂生芝，佞諛尤甚。」

translations.literal: That winter Qin Hui died. Emperor Gaozong said: "In recent years the four quarters have reported auspicious signs, embellishing words to please their superiors—as when Lin Ji of Xin prefecture memorialized that lingzhi grew at the ancestral temple of Qin Hui's father; such flattery was especially gross."
translations.idiomatic: That winter Qin Hui died. Emperor Gaozong said: "In recent years the four quarters have reported auspicious signs, dressing up words to please their superiors—as when Lin Ji of Xin prefecture memorialized that lingzhi grew at the ancestral temple of Qin Hui's father; such sycophancy was especially gross."

sentences.zh: 明年四月甲午，詔郡國無獻瑞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, on jiawu, an edict forbade the commanderies and kingdoms to present auspicious portents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year, on jiawu, an edict forbade the commanderies and kingdoms to present auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年七月，池州竹生穗，實如米，饑民采之以食，守臣魯詧爲《野穀生竹圖》以獻。

translations.literal: In Qiandao 1, seventh month, bamboo in Chizhou produced ears, and its grains were like rice; hungry people gathered them for food, and the local official Lu Cha presented a Picture of Wild Grain Growing from Bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qiandao 1, bamboo in Chizhou put forth ears with grains like rice, which famine-stricken people gathered for food. The local official Lu Cha presented a Picture of Wild Grain Growing from Bamboo.

sentences.zh: 御史劾詧不以民食草木爲病，坐佞免官。

translations.literal: A censor impeached Cha for not treating the people eating grasses and trees as a hardship; he was dismissed from office for sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: A censor impeached Lu Cha for failing to regard people reduced to eating grasses and trees as a calamity, and he was dismissed for flattery.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年八月，太室西北夾室楹生白芝，四葉，前史以白芝爲喪祥。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Qingyuan, white lingzhi of four leaves grew on a pillar in the side chamber northwest of the Grand Chamber; earlier histories regarded white lingzhi as an omen of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Qingyuan, white lingzhi of four leaves grew on a pillar in the side chamber northwest of the Grand Chamber; earlier histories had taken white lingzhi as an omen of mourning.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，國連有大喪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, the state suffered mourning upon mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the following year, the state suffered one great funeral after another.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年十一月，秘書省右文殿楹生芝二莖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jiatai, two stalks of lingzhi grew on a pillar of the Youwen Hall in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jiatai, two stalks of lingzhi grew on a pillar of the Youwen Hall in the Secretariat.
